name: Egocentric-10K
notes: First-person factory work, monocular head camera, no audio. Stream it; do not download. Commercial use permitted.
covers: first-person footage of factory workers' hands: picking, placing, assembling, fastening, sorting and packing parts, using hand tools

name: Egocentric-10K (Voxel51 subset)
notes: Ungated prototyping subset of Egocentric-10K. H.264, so ffmpeg can pull frames straight off the URL. Start here.
covers: a small sample of Egocentric-10K: factory workers' hands picking, placing, assembling and using hand tools

name: Egocentric-100K
covers: the same kind of first-person factory footage as Egocentric-10K, ten times as much

name: EgoDex
notes: Apple Vision Pro capture at 1080p/30Hz with 3D pose for every hand joint, plus language annotations and camera extrinsics. Named in the hackathon brief for pick-and-place. Download from GitHub, not the Hub.
covers: tabletop dexterous manipulation of everyday objects with every hand joint tracked: picking and placing, opening and closing containers, inserting, pouring, folding, sorting

name: Ego-Exo4D
notes: Paired first- and third-person views of skilled activity. Non-commercial; needs a signed licence.
covers: skilled activities filmed first- and third-person: cooking, bike repair, health procedures, music, sports, dance

name: EPIC-KITCHENS-100
notes: The classic egocentric benchmark. Densely labelled verb-noun action segments -- a ready-made source of action titles.
covers: unscripted home kitchen activity labelled verb by verb: take, put, open, close, wash, cut, peel, pour, mix, stir, scoop, spread, wipe

name: SO-101 Pick & Place
notes: Real teleoperated pick-and-place in LeRobot v3 format. Videos are AV1 -- frame extraction needs an ffmpeg built with libdav1d.
covers: a low-cost SO-101 arm teleoperated to pick objects up and place them

name: SO-100 Sorting
notes: Sorting into bins. Useful as a second task for composition experiments.
covers: an SO-100 arm teleoperated to sort objects into bins

name: ALOHA Insertion (image)
notes: Stores frames as images rather than video, so the Hub viewer serves thumbnails directly -- no ffmpeg, no codec trouble.
covers: simulated two-arm ALOHA robot inserting a peg into a socket

name: High Quality Folding
notes: Deformable-object manipulation. Hard task, good contrast against rigid pick-and-place.
covers: teleoperated robot folding cloth and garments

name: DROID 1.0.1
notes: Large-scale multi-scene Franka manipulation. A pi0.5 fine-tuning target exists for it.
covers: a Franka arm teleoperated through everyday tasks in many homes and labs: picking, placing, opening drawers and doors, wiping, pouring

name: Spirit Moz1 Pick & Place
notes: Not public on the Hub -- obtain from Spirit after-sales support with a key. Lands in the LeRobot cache at ~/.cache/huggingface/lerobot/spirit-ai/pickplace and is what pi05_moz trains on. Ask the organizers on day one.
